acknowledge.en: to accept that something is true
acknowledge.ex: The company acknowledged its mistake publicly.

action.en: something done, here strikes by workers
action.ex: The council promised quick action on the roads.
action.zh: 行動（industrial action：勞工抗爭行動）

add.en: to put more of something in
add.ex: You can add more water if needed.

adding.en: adding to: making something bigger or worse
adding.ex: Adding to the problem, the bus broke down.

additional.ex: The school needs additional teachers next year.

addressing.ex: She is addressing the students this morning.

affordable.en: not too expensive to pay for
affordable.ex: Young people want more affordable homes.

ago.ex: I moved here two years ago.

agreed.ex: The neighbours agreed a time for the meeting.

agreement.ex: Both countries signed a trade agreement.

allocated.ex: The city allocated money for new parks.

example.en: The council allocated more money to road repairs.
example.zh: 議會撥了更多經費給道路維修。

note.usage: allocate sth to/for sth；常用於預算、資源分配。

noteEn.meaning: to give money or things for a particular purpose.

noteEs.exampleTr: El ayuntamiento asignó más dinero a la reparación de carreteras.
noteEs.usage: allocate algo to/for algo; habitual con presupuestos.

noteHi.exampleTr: परिषद ने सड़क मरम्मत के लिए अधिक धन आवंटित किया।
noteHi.usage: allocate sth to/for sth; बजट और संसाधनों के लिए।

noteJa.exampleTr: 議会は道路補修により多くの予算を割り当てた。
noteJa.usage: allocate A to/for B。予算や資源について使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 의회는 도로 보수에 더 많은 예산을 배정했다.
noteKo.usage: allocate A to/for B 형태로 예산·자원에 쓴다.

also.ex: She speaks French and also Spanish.

anticipated.ex: The concert was bigger than anticipated.

any.en: one or some, no matter which

approach.en: a way of dealing with something
approach.ex: We need a new approach to teaching maths.

approximately.en: close to a number, not exact
approximately.ex: The trip takes approximately three hours.

argued.ex: He argued that taxes were too high.

around.ex: Around fifty people came to the party.

as.en: used to compare, give reasons or roles

aside.en: set aside: keep for a purpose
aside.ex: Put aside some money each week.

aspire.ex: Many students aspire to work abroad.

at.en: in or near a place or time

attention.ex: The story got a lot of attention online.

basic.ex: They learned basic first aid at school.

be.en: to exist or have a quality

become.ex: The town has become very popular with tourists.

began.ex: The film began at eight o'clock.

better.ex: The new phone has a better camera.

breakthrough.ex: Scientists made a breakthrough in cancer research.

budget.ex: The school budget is very small this year.

called.ex: The match was called off because of rain.

callinan.en: Kevin Callinan, head of the union Fórsa

cancel.ex: We had to cancel our holiday.

cave.en: cave in: give in to pressure
cave.ex: The manager refused to cave in to their demands.

cent.ex: Prices went up by five per cent this year.

central.ex: Health is central to a happy life.

change.ex: I want to change my job next year.

close.en: to make a gap smaller or end it
close.ex: The school wants to close the gap between students.

come.ex: More help will come next week.

commemoration.en: an event to remember a person or event
commemoration.ex: A commemoration was held for the soldiers.

comment.ex: The police did not comment on the case.

commission.en: an official group with a special job
commission.ex: The commission will report next month.

commitments.ex: The firm made commitments to cut waste.

compensate.en: to make up for a loss
compensate.ex: Nothing can compensate for lost time.

example.en: Extra holidays can compensate for long working hours.
example.zh: 額外的假期可以彌補長工時。

note.usage: compensate (sb) for sth；表示彌補損失或不足。

noteEn.meaning: to make up for a loss or lack.

noteEs.exampleTr: Las vacaciones extra pueden compensar las largas jornadas.
noteEs.usage: compensate (a alguien) for algo; reparar una pérdida.

noteHi.exampleTr: अतिरिक्त छुट्टियाँ लंबे काम के घंटों की भरपाई कर सकती हैं।
noteHi.usage: compensate (sb) for sth; नुकसान की भरपाई के लिए।

noteJa.exampleTr: 休暇を増やせば長時間労働を埋め合わせられる。
noteJa.meaning: 補う；埋め合わせる；補償する。
noteJa.usage: compensate (人) for ～ で損失や不足を補う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 추가 휴가가 긴 근무 시간을 보상할 수 있다.

concede.en: to admit something is true, often unwillingly
concede.ex: He conceded that the plan had some problems.

concluded.ex: The two countries concluded a trade deal.

conclusion.en: the end or final result of something
conclusion.ex: The meeting came to a quick conclusion.

consequently.ex: It rained all day; consequently, the match was cancelled.

example.en: Fuel prices rose; consequently, fewer people drove to work.
example.zh: 油價上漲，因此開車上班的人變少了。

note.usage: 連接副詞，常置句首加逗號，表示前文造成的結果；學術寫作常用。

noteEs.exampleTr: El combustible subió; por consiguiente, menos gente fue en coche al trabajo.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir al inicio de la frase con coma para indicar un resultado.

noteHi.exampleTr: ईंधन के दाम बढ़े; इसलिए कम लोग गाड़ी से काम पर गए।
noteHi.usage: वाक्य की शुरुआत में अल्पविराम के साथ परिणाम बताने के लिए।

noteJa.exampleTr: 燃料価格が上がり、その結果、車通勤の人が減った。
noteJa.usage: 文頭にコンマと共に置き、前の内容の結果を示す。

noteKo.exampleTr: 연료 가격이 올랐고, 그 결과 차로 출근하는 사람이 줄었다.
noteKo.usage: 문장 앞에 쉼표와 함께 써서 결과를 나타낸다.

considerably.ex: Prices have risen considerably this year.

constitutes.ex: This decision constitutes a big change.

consult.en: to ask someone for advice or opinions
consult.ex: You should consult a doctor first.

contain.en: to have something inside or as part

contended.ex: She contended that the rule was unfair.

contingency.en: a possible future event to plan for
contingency.ex: Keep some money for any contingency.

contingent.ex: The trip is contingent on good weather.

example.en: The offer is contingent upon a successful interview.
example.zh: 這份錄用取決於面試是否成功。

note.usage: 常用 contingent on/upon sth，表示某事成立的前提條件；屬正式學術用語。

noteEn.meaning: depending on something else happening first.
noteEn.usage: Use 'contingent on/upon something'; it is formal.

noteEs.exampleTr: La oferta depende de que la entrevista salga bien.
noteEs.meaning: que depende de algo; condicionado a.
noteEs.usage: Se usa contingent on/upon algo para expresar una condición; registro formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: यह प्रस्ताव सफल साक्षात्कार पर निर्भर है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी और बात पर निर्भर; सशर्त।
noteHi.usage: contingent on/upon sth के रूप में शर्त बताने के लिए प्रयोग होता है।

noteJa.exampleTr: その採用はうまく面接を通ることが条件だ。
noteJa.usage: contingent on/upon ～ で「～を条件とする」。硬い書き言葉。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 제안은 면접 합격을 조건으로 한다.
noteKo.usage: contingent on/upon ~ 형태로 조건을 나타내며 격식체이다.

day.ex: The shop is closed for one day.

deal.ex: The two companies signed a deal.

decided.ex: We decided to stay at home.

decline.en: a fall in amount or quality
decline.ex: There was a decline in visitor numbers.

declined.ex: She declined to answer the question.
declined.zh: 拒絕（declined to comment：拒絕評論）

deferring.ex: They are deferring the decision until spring.

delegation.en: a group sent to represent others
delegation.ex: A delegation from Japan visited the school.

department.en: a part of a government or organisation
department.ex: She works in the finance department.

described.ex: She described the film as boring.

designed.en: made or planned for a purpose
designed.ex: This course is designed for beginners.
designed.ja: 〜するよう作られた；意図された

discuss.ex: We need to discuss the plan.

discussed.ex: They discussed the problem for hours.

discussion.ex: The plan is still under discussion.

dismissed.en: said something is not true or important
dismissed.ex: She dismissed the rumours as nonsense.

divert.en: to move attention to something else
divert.ex: He told a joke to divert attention.

do.en: to perform an action; also a helping verb

down.ex: The guards were told to stand down.

drawn.ex: The money was drawn from savings.
drawn.zh: 提取（drawn from：從…撥出）；被引誘表態（drawn on）

due.ex: The train is due to arrive at six.
due.zh: 預定的（was due to：預定要）

earlier.en: before the present or another time
earlier.zh: 較早的；先前（weeks earlier：幾週前）

earmarked.en: set aside for a particular purpose
earmarked.ex: The money is earmarked for new schools.
earmarked.ja: （特定用途に）割り当てられた

example.en: Ten million euro was earmarked for new schools.
example.zh: 一千萬歐元被指定用於興建新學校。

note.meaning: 指定（款項）用於某用途；撥出。
note.usage: 常用被動 be earmarked for sth，表示資金已預留給特定用途。

noteEn.meaning: to set money aside for a special use.

noteEs.exampleTr: Se destinaron diez millones de euros a nuevas escuelas.
noteEs.meaning: destinar o asignar (dinero) a un fin concreto.
noteEs.usage: Se usa mucho en pasiva: be earmarked for algo.

noteHi.exampleTr: नए स्कूलों के लिए एक करोड़ यूरो निर्धारित किए गए।
noteHi.meaning: किसी खास काम के लिए धन अलग रखना।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर कर्मवाच्य में: be earmarked for sth।

noteJa.exampleTr: 1000万ユーロが新しい学校に充てられた。
noteJa.meaning: （資金を）特定の用途に充てる。
noteJa.usage: 受け身 be earmarked for ～ の形が多い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 천만 유로가 새 학교 건립에 배정되었다.
noteKo.usage: 수동태 be earmarked for ~ 형태가 흔하다.

efficient.en: working well without wasting time or money
efficient.ex: Trains are an efficient way to travel.

element.ex: Trust is an important element of friendship.

emphasised.en: said something strongly to show importance
emphasised.ex: She emphasised the need for safety.

employees.en: people who work for a company

end.ex: The film ends at ten o'clock.

erosion.en: slow loss or weakening over time
erosion.ex: Inflation causes an erosion of savings.

example.en: Rising prices caused an erosion of savings.
example.zh: 物價上漲使儲蓄逐漸縮水。

note.usage: 原指土壤被侵蝕，引申為價值、權利逐漸減少；常見 erosion of pay/trust。

noteEn.meaning: a slow loss or weakening of something.
noteEn.usage: Used for value or rights: 'erosion of pay'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La subida de precios causó una erosión de los ahorros.
noteEs.usage: Pérdida lenta de valor o derechos: erosion of pay/trust.

noteHi.exampleTr: बढ़ती कीमतों से बचत का क्षरण हुआ।
noteHi.meaning: धीरे-धीरे घटना या कमज़ोर होना; क्षरण।
noteHi.usage: मूल्य या अधिकारों की धीमी कमी के लिए: erosion of pay/trust।

noteJa.exampleTr: 物価上昇で貯金が目減りした。
noteJa.usage: 価値や権利が少しずつ失われること。erosion of pay/trust。

noteKo.usage: 가치나 권리가 서서히 줄어드는 것: erosion of pay/trust.

estimated.ex: The trip is estimated to cost €500.

estimates.en: calculations that are close but not exact
estimates.ex: Early estimates show a small rise.

excluded.en: left out or not allowed in
excluded.ex: No option has been excluded yet.
excluded.ja: 除外した；締め出された

expenditure.en: money spent, often by a government
expenditure.ex: Public expenditure on health keeps rising.

extra.ex: We need extra chairs for the party.

fact.ex: It is a fact that water boils at 100°C.

factored.ex: Once travel is factored in, the trip costs more.

far.en: very much; not at all (in 'far from')
far.ex: The job is far from finished.
far.zh: 遠遠（far from guaranteed：遠不能保證）

faster.ex: Prices are rising faster than wages.

few.ja: 少しの（a few：いくつかの）

fianna.en: part of the name of an Irish political party
fianna.ja: フィアナ（フィアナ・フォイル党）

figures.ex: The latest figures show a rise.
figures.zh: 數字；數據（senior figures：高層人士）

finish.ex: We hope to finish by Friday.

fix.ex: We need to fix this problem quickly.

follow.ex: Heavy rain will follow the storm tonight.

for.en: used to show purpose or who gets something

formal.en: official and done in the proper way
formal.ex: The company sent a formal letter to its staff.

framework.ex: The two sides agreed a framework for future talks.

fraught.ex: The meeting was fraught with arguments.

frequently.ex: She frequently works late on Fridays.

from.en: showing where something starts or comes

fronted.en: be fronted by: be led or represented by
fronted.ex: The campaign is fronted by a famous singer.

fund.en: an amount of money kept for a purpose
fund.ex: The school has a fund for new books.

fundamental.ex: Clean water is a fundamental human need.

funding.ex: The club needs more funding for new equipment.

funds.ex: The charity raised funds for the hospital.

further.ex: Call us if you need further information.

furthermore.ex: The flat is cheap; furthermore, it is near work.

fáil.en: part of the party name Fianna Fáil
fáil.ja: （政党名フィアナ・フォイルの一部）

gains.ex: The new machines brought big gains in speed.

gap.ex: The gap between rich and poor is growing.

general.en: main or chief (in a job title)
general.ex: She was elected general manager last year.

gone.ex: The price of bread has gone up again.

good.ex: This is a good place to study.

got.ex: The meeting got under way at ten.

government.en: the group of people who run a country
government.ex: The government will build new schools.

government's.ex: The government's plan was announced today.

grievance.en: a reason for complaining about unfair treatment
grievance.ex: Low pay is the main grievance of the nurses.

example.en: Staff raised their grievance with the manager.
example.zh: 員工向經理提出了他們的不滿。

note.usage: 指對不公平待遇的正式不滿；常見 air/address a grievance、a long-standing grievance。

noteEs.exampleTr: El personal presentó su queja al gerente.
noteEs.usage: Queja formal por un trato injusto; address a grievance.

noteHi.exampleTr: कर्मचारियों ने प्रबंधक के सामने अपनी शिकायत रखी।
noteHi.usage: अनुचित व्यवहार की औपचारिक शिकायत; address a grievance आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 職員は上司に不満を申し立てた。
noteJa.usage: 不当な扱いへの正式な不満。address a grievance などの形で使う。

noteKo.usage: 부당한 대우에 대한 공식 불만으로 address a grievance 형태가 흔하다.

guaranteed.ex: Success is not guaranteed, but we will try.

had.ex: We had a long meeting yesterday.

happy.ex: The workers were not happy with the offer.

have.en: to own or hold; also helps form tenses
have.ex: We have three cats at home.

help.en: to make something easier for someone
help.ex: Can you help me carry these bags?

hope.ex: We hope to finish the work today.

hopes.ex: She hopes to visit Japan next year.

how.ex: Show me how this machine works.

if.en: used to talk about a possible situation

in.en: inside; at a place or time

include.ex: The price does not include breakfast.

increases.en: rises in amount, e.g. pay rises
increases.ex: Workers want pay increases this year.

indicated.ex: He indicated that he might change his mind.

industrial.en: industrial action: strikes and protests by workers
industrial.ex: Nurses are planning industrial action next month.

inflation.ex: High inflation makes food more expensive.

insisted.ex: She insisted that she was right.

intended.ex: The money is intended for new books.

larger.ex: They moved to a larger house.

lead.en: to be in charge of a group
lead.ex: She will lead the team next season.

leader.en: the person in charge of a group
leader.ex: The leader spoke to the press.

leaks.en: secret information given to the media

led.ex: The rain led us to cancel the trip.

lines.en: picket lines: groups of striking workers outside work
lines.ex: Strikers stood on the lines in the rain.

listening.en: paying attention to what people say
listening.ex: The teacher is listening to the students.

long.ex: They have long wanted a new park.

longer.ex: The days get longer in spring.

lost.en: had something taken away; no longer have
lost.ex: She lost her phone on the bus.

low-paid.ex: Many low-paid workers struggle to pay rent.

lower-paid.ex: Lower-paid staff will get a bigger rise.

lowest.ex: This shop has the lowest prices in town.
lowest.zh: 最低的（the lowest paid：收入最低者）

made.en: caused to be (made clear: said clearly)
made.ex: The teacher made the rules clear on day one.

martin.en: surname of the Irish prime minister

meanwhile.ex: I cooked dinner; meanwhile, my brother set the table.

measures.en: actions taken to deal with something
measures.ex: The school took measures to save energy.

members.en: people who belong to a group

micheál.en: first name of the Irish prime minister

money.en: cash; value for money: worth the cost
money.ex: I saved money for a new bike.

more.en: a larger amount; to a greater degree

must.ex: You must wear a seatbelt in the car.

need.ex: You need a ticket to enter.

negotiations.en: formal talks to reach an agreement

nevertheless.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went for a walk.

example.en: The test was hard; nevertheless, most students passed.
example.zh: 考試很難，儘管如此，大多數學生都及格了。

note.usage: 表示讓步轉折，語氣比 but 正式；常置句首或分號後。

noteEn.usage: More formal than 'but'; often after a semicolon.

noteEs.exampleTr: El examen era difícil; no obstante, casi todos aprobaron.
noteEs.usage: Más formal que but; va al inicio o tras punto y coma.

noteHi.exampleTr: परीक्षा कठिन थी; फिर भी अधिकांश छात्र पास हुए।
noteHi.usage: but से अधिक औपचारिक; वाक्य की शुरुआत या अर्धविराम के बाद।

noteJa.exampleTr: 試験は難しかったが、それでもほとんどの学生が合格した。
noteJa.meaning: それにもかかわらず；しかしながら。
noteJa.usage: but より改まった語。文頭やセミコロンの後に置く。

noteKo.exampleTr: 시험은 어려웠지만 그럼에도 대부분의 학생이 합격했다.
noteKo.usage: but보다 격식 있으며 문장 앞이나 세미콜론 뒤에 쓴다.

new.ex: She bought a new coat for winter.

non-negotiable.ex: Safety rules on the site are non-negotiable.
non-negotiable.zh: 不可談判的；不容讓步的

not.ex: I am not hungry right now.

objective.ex: Our main objective is to finish by Friday.

obscure.ex: Clouds obscured the view of the mountains.

obtained.ex: She obtained a visa to work abroad.

off.en: used in phrases like called off, worse off
off.ex: The concert was called off because of rain.
off.ja: 中止；暮らし向きが悪い
off.zh: called off：取消；worse off：境況變差

on.en: used for days, topics and places

open.ex: She is open to new ideas.

opened.ex: The meeting opened with a short speech.

openness.ex: The team showed openness to new ideas.

opposed.ex: Many residents opposed the new road.

out.en: ruled out: said it will not happen
out.ex: The coach ruled out any changes to the team.

outpaced.ex: Online sales outpaced shop sales last year.

over.zh: 在…期間（over the weekend：週末期間）

paid.ex: The lowest paid workers need help most.
paid.zh: 薪酬（the lowest paid：收入最低者）

paramount.ex: Safety is paramount on a building site.

example.en: Patient safety is paramount in every hospital.
example.zh: 在每家醫院，病人安全都是最重要的。

note.usage: 通常作表語：be paramount；比 most important 正式。

noteEs.exampleTr: La seguridad del paciente es primordial en todo hospital.
noteEs.usage: Suele ir tras be: be paramount; of paramount importance.

noteHi.exampleTr: हर अस्पताल में मरीज़ की सुरक्षा सर्वोपरि है।
noteHi.usage: प्रायः be paramount के रूप में; of paramount importance आम है।

noteJa.exampleTr: どの病院でも患者の安全が最優先だ。
noteJa.usage: be paramount、of paramount importance の形で使う。

noteKo.usage: be paramount, of paramount importance 형태로 쓴다.

pay.ex: The nurses asked for better pay.

picket.ex: Nurses stood on the picket line all day.

plain.en: plain sailing: easy, with no problems
plain.ex: The exam was plain and simple.

plan.en: an idea of what to do
plan.ex: We made a plan for the weekend.

planned.ex: The planned trip was cancelled because of rain.

poised.ex: The team is poised to win the cup.

possibility.ex: There is a possibility of rain tomorrow.

postponed.ex: The match was postponed because of snow.

postponement.en: moving something to a later time

postponing.ex: They are postponing the wedding until spring.

pot.en: an amount of money for a purpose
pot.ex: The class has a pot of money for a trip.

power.en: ability (purchasing power: what money can buy)
power.ex: High prices reduce the power of your wages.

prepared.ex: Are you prepared for the test?

previously.ex: She previously worked in a bank.

principle.ex: Honesty is an important principle for me.

process.en: a series of steps to reach a result
process.ex: The hiring process took two months.

productivity.en: how much useful work is done
productivity.ex: New tools raised productivity in the office.

prolonged.en: lasting a long time, longer than expected
prolonged.ex: A prolonged dry spell hurt the farmers.

prompted.ex: The storm prompted the school to close early.

protect.en: keep someone or something safe from harm
protect.ex: Sun cream helps protect your skin.

protects.ex: A strong lock protects your home.

protracted.ex: After protracted talks, the two sides signed a deal.

example.en: The protracted dispute closed the factory for months.
example.zh: 這場曠日持久的爭議讓工廠停工數月。

note.usage: 多修飾負面且耗時的事，如 protracted negotiations/dispute。

noteEn.meaning: lasting longer than expected or wanted.
noteEn.usage: Used for long, difficult things: 'protracted talks'.

paragraphs: Public sector workers and the Government began pay talks on Monday. Before the talks, the Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, spoke about them.
He said any new pay deal must help workers do more and better work. He also wants good value for public money.
Unions say prices have gone up faster than pay since 2021. They want to close a gap of 5 to 7 per cent.
The budget has €1.2 billion for a pay deal. Some reports say more money could come. Martin said nothing is decided yet.
A strike planned for Wednesday was stopped. But one union, Unite, may still strike. The Government hopes the talks will end in a few weeks.

Pay talks between the Government and public sector trade unions began on Monday at the Workplace Relations Commission. Both sides agreed a basic plan for the talks over the weekend, so a strike planned for Wednesday was called off.

On Sunday, the Taoiseach, Micheál Martin, said that any new deal must include ways to improve productivity. In other words, workers would need to change how they work so that public services become better and more efficient. He said the Government wants good value for money and also wants to protect low-paid workers.
The unions say most workers have lost between 5 and 7 per cent of their pay since 2021, because prices rose faster than wages. They want the new deal to fix this.

The recent budget set aside €1.2 billion for a pay deal. Some reports say the Government could add money from a separate €1.6 billion fund. Martin would not discuss these reports and said no figures had been decided.

Kevin Callinan, the leader of the union Fórsa, will lead the union team. He said the Government had told him it was listening to workers on the picket lines, and the unions would now see if that was true.

Not every union is happy. Unite, which has about 4,000 members in the public sector, voted against stopping the strike and could still take action. Government sources expect difficult talks that may last longer than a few weeks.

Formal pay negotiations between the Government and public service trade unions opened on Monday at the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC). The talks follow a framework agreement reached over the weekend, which led unions to cancel a second day of strike action planned for Wednesday.

Speaking on Sunday at a Fianna Fáil commemoration in Bodenstown, Co Kildare, Taoiseach Micheál Martin insisted that any deal must contain productivity measures. He described value for money and productivity as central to the Government's position, and said he was open to an affordable agreement that also protects lower-paid staff.
Unions are seeking to recover a shortfall of between 5 and 7 per cent in real pay since 2021, as inflation has outpaced the increases most workers received.

The recent budget allocated €1.2 billion for a new agreement, and there has been speculation that extra funds could be drawn from a €1.6 billion contingency reserve. Mr Martin refused to comment, saying nothing had been decided. Fórsa general secretary Kevin Callinan, who will lead the union side, suggested the reported figures were intended to distract from the €2 billion the Government had discussed only weeks earlier.

The Government will be represented by officials from the Department of Public Expenditure, a department with which unions have had a tense relationship. Senior sources expect tough negotiations and hope to finish within weeks, although they are prepared for a longer process.
Meanwhile, Unite, which represents around 4,000 public sector workers, opposed postponing the strike and was due to consult its shop stewards on Monday.

Pay negotiations between the Government and public service unions got under way on Monday at the Workplace Relations Commission, after a weekend breakthrough on a framework for talks prompted unions to stand down a second day of industrial action scheduled for Wednesday.

Addressing a Fianna Fáil commemoration at Bodenstown, Co Kildare, on Sunday, Taoiseach Micheál Martin made clear that productivity gains would be a non-negotiable element of any settlement. He dismissed suggestions that he was poised to cave in to union demands, stressing that value for money remained paramount, though he signalled openness to an affordable deal that would safeguard the lowest paid.
The unions' central grievance is an erosion of real pay: once inflation is factored in, most public servants are estimated to be 5 to 7 per cent worse off than in 2021.

While €1.2 billion has been earmarked in the budget, reports have suggested the pot could be topped up from a €1.6 billion contingency fund. Mr Martin declined to be drawn on the figures. Fórsa's general secretary, Kevin Callinan, who will spearhead the union delegation, contended that such leaks were designed to obscure the fact that €2 billion had been under discussion only weeks ago.

The talks are unlikely to be plain sailing. The State's side will be fronted by the Department of Public Expenditure, with which unions have long had a fraught relationship, and senior figures concede that a swift conclusion is far from guaranteed.
Adding to the uncertainty, Unite, which represents some 4,000 public sector staff, voted against deferring the strike and has not ruled out further action.

Taoiseach Micheál Martin stated on Sunday that any agreement would be contingent upon substantial productivity commitments. He emphasised that value for money constitutes a fundamental principle of the Government's approach; nevertheless, he indicated a willingness to reach an affordable settlement that would protect lower-paid employees.

The unions' principal objective is to compensate for a significant decline in real earnings. According to their estimates, inflation has reduced the purchasing power of most public servants by between 5 and 7 per cent since 2021.

With regard to funding, the budget allocated €1.2 billion to a new agreement, and it has been speculated that additional resources could be obtained from a €1.6 billion contingency fund. The Taoiseach declined to comment on these figures. Kevin Callinan, general secretary of Fórsa, who will lead the union delegation, argued that the reports were intended to divert attention from the considerably larger sum of €2 billion discussed previously.

It is widely anticipated that the negotiations will be protracted. The Government will be represented by the Department of Public Expenditure, with which relations have frequently been strained, and although officials aspire to reach a conclusion within weeks, they acknowledge that the process may be prolonged.
Furthermore, Unite, which represents approximately 4,000 public sector workers, opposed the postponement and has not excluded the possibility of further strikes.
